docs.text: HardFOC driver ADS9324 Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the Texas Instruments ADS9324 16-channel, 16-bit simultaneous-sampling SAR ADC. It brings the chip up in 1-lane SDOUT mode, programs each channel's PGA range, input type, filter and calibration, and reads all 16 channels from one CONVST edge, on any MCU with an SPI controller and two GPIOs. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a class that runs one SPI transfer with chip select held low, and a class that drives CONVST, reads DRDY and waits; it does the rest: the initialisation sequence, register banks, 24-bit frames, PGA nibble packing, the conversion burst and the conversion to volts. 16-channel simultaneous-sampling SAR ADC with analog front end ADS9324 Texas Instruments Conversion 16 SAR ADCs, 16 bits, up to 1 MSPS per channel, all sampled on the CONVST falling edge Inputs 1 MΩ PGA per channel: differential, single-ended or open-wire safe; ±2.5, ±5, ±6.25, ±10, ±12.5 V Interface SPI mode 0 up to 60 MHz, 24-bit register frames; conversion data on 1, 2, 4 or 8 lanes Control pins CONVST, DRDY/ALARM, RESET (active low), REFSEL Supply AVDD_5V 4.75 V to 5.25 V, AVDD_1V8 1.7 V to 1.9 V, IOVDD 1.7 V to 3.6 V; internal 4.096 V reference Package 64-pin VQFN (RSK), 8 mm × 8 mm, –40 °C to +125 °C Driver mode 1-lane, 16-bit conversion data on SDOUT (GEN_CFG3 = 0x0032 ), sharing the register SPI bus Datasheet (SBASB22) · Product page What you get ¶ One object per chip. ADS9324<Spi, Host> owns the register banks, the 24-bit frames and the cached channel settings. See API guide . Bring-up in one call. EnsureInitialized() waits for the supplies, resets the chip, selects 1-lane SDOUT output and checks DEVICE_ID. See Quickstart . A front end per channel. Range, input type, filter bandwidth, offset and gain for each of the 16 inputs, plus the on-chip ADC calibration. See PGA and calibration . Oversampling. The block-average filter, 2 to 128 samples per snapshot. See API guide . Simultaneous snapshots in volts. ReadSnapshot() pulses CONVST, waits for DRDY and returns 16 counts and 16 voltages, each scaled with its channel's range. See Registers and SPI frames . Zero-overhead portability. The port is two CRTP classes: no virtual calls, no heap, no RTOS dependency. See Porting . Tested without hardware. Host tests run the driver against a model of the register file. See Testing and CI . Where to go next ¶ Quickstart Wire the chip, write the port, read 16 channels in about 15 lines. Hardware Pins, supplies, bus settings and the timing the driver relies on. API guide ¶ How to do the common jobs with the driver: initialise, configure channels, calibrate, read and handle errors. Every snippet on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/api_tasks.cpp , with adc an ads9324::ADS9324<MySpi, MyHost> over the port . The API reference lists every member. The shape of the API ¶ One ADS9324<Spi, Host> object per chip. Its methods fall into these groups: Group Methods Bring-up EnsureInitialized() , IsInitialized() , SoftwareReset() , HardwareReset() , ReadDeviceId() , SetReference() Channels ConfigureChannel() , ConfigureAllChannels() , GetChannelConfig() , SetChannelOffset() , SetChannelGain() Calibration SetSystemCorrection() , RunAdcCalibration() , GetAdcCalMode() , OffsetCorrectionFor() , GainCorrectionFor() Data interface SetDataFormat() , GetDataFormat() , SetDigitalInterface() , SetChannelCountMode() , SetOversampling() Pins and power SetAlarmPin() , ProgramWindowComparator() , SetPowerDown() Reading ReadSnapshot() , ReadChannel() , CountToVoltage() , GetDiagnostics() Configuration calls return bool : false means the channel index was out of range or the call did not complete. Reads return a Snapshot or ReadResult with an error field. Nothing throws or allocates. Channels are numbered 0 to 15 in the API (AIN1 to AIN16 on the chip). Initialise ¶ if ( ! adc . EnsureInitialized ()) { // 30 ms settle, SW reset, GEN_CFG3 = 0x0032, DEVICE_ID, PGA // defaults const uint16_t id = adc . ReadDeviceId (); // 0x0004 on a healthy ADS9324, 0 when SDOUT is dead std :: printf ( "ADS9324 init failed, DEVICE_ID = 0x%04X 
 " , id ); return false ; } // Later calls return at once; EnsureInitialized(true) runs the whole sequence again. EnsureInitialized() runs the datasheet's 1-lane sequence ( Registers and SPI frames ) and fails when DEVICE_ID is not 0x0004 . Every read and every snapshot needs it to have succeeded. Define CONFIG_ADS9324_SKIP_DEVICE_ID_CHECK to skip the ID check during bench bring-up ( Configuration ). Reset and reference ¶ // Use the internal 4.096 V reference whatever the REFSEL pin is strapped to. if ( ! adc . SetReference ( ads9324 :: ReferenceSource :: Internal )) { return false ; } // Pulse the RESET pin (the port has ResetWrite()); fall back to SW_RST otherwise. const bool reset_ok = Adc :: HasHardwareReset () ? adc . HardwareReset () : adc . SoftwareReset (); // Both resets return the reference to RefselPin: select it again. return reset_ok && adc . SetReference ( ads9324 :: ReferenceSource :: Internal ); SoftwareReset() writes SW_RST; HardwareReset() pulses the RESET pin (low for RESET_PULSE_US , then the 30 ms t PU ) and needs the optional ResetWrite() hook in the port ( HasHardwareReset() tells you at compile time). Either reset returns every register to its reset value; the driver then selects 1-lane SDOUT again and writes the channel defaults, so offsets, gains, the window comparator, the channel-count mode, the reference selection, the oversampling filter and the ADC_CAL correction are back at their reset values. If that reprogramming fails, IsInitialized() turns false . SetReference() writes ANA_CFG1 (Table 7-3): ReferenceSource ANA_CFG1 Reference RefselPin (reset) 0x0000 REFSEL pin: high = internal, low = external on REFIO Internal 0x0002 Internal 4.096 V, REFSEL ignored External 0x0003 External on REFIO, REFSEL ignored; without one the chip powers down Configure the channels ¶ // AIN1..AIN4: ±10 V differential, wide bandwidth for a fast current-sense signal. ads9324 :: ChannelConfig current ; current . type = ads9324 :: InputType :: Differential ; current . range = ads9324 :: InputRange :: PlusMinus10V ; current . bandwidth = ads9324 :: PgaBandwidth :: Wide ; // AIN5..AIN16: ±2.5 V single-ended sensors that may come unplugged. ads9324 :: ChannelConfig sensor ; sensor . type = ads9324 :: InputType :: SingleEndedOpenWireSafe ; sensor . range = ads9324 :: InputRange :: PlusMinus2V5 ; for ( uint8_t ch = 0 ; ch < ads9324 :: kNumChannels ; ++ ch ) { if ( ! adc . ConfigureChannel ( ch , ch < 4 ? current : sensor )) { return false ; // ch out of range, or the bus failed } } ChannelConfig field Default Values type Differential Differential , SingleEnded , SingleEndedOpenWireSafe range PlusMinus5V PlusMinus2V5 , PlusMinus5V , PlusMinus6V25 , PlusMinus10V , PlusMinus12V5 bandwidth Low Low (25.5 kHz), Wide (280 kHz to 350 kHz) common_mode_correct false Common-mode error correction Each ConfigureChannel() call is a read-modify-write of two registers (about eight SPI frames). The driver keeps the last configuration per channel; GetChannelConfig(ch) returns it, and the voltage conversion uses its range. EnsureInitialized() and SoftwareReset() write the compile-time defaults ( DefaultChannelConfig() : ±5 V differential, low bandwidth unless changed with CONFIG_ADS9324_* , see Configuration ) to all 16 channels, so the chip and the driver agree from the start. PGA and calibration explains the encodings. Calibrate offset and gain ¶ // Offset: 10-bit two's complement in quarter LSBs (-512..511), added before the gain (Equation // 1). Channel 0 reads 10 LSB high with its input shorted: subtract 40 quarter LSBs. if ( ! adc . SetChannelOffset ( 0 , -40 )) { return false ; } // Gain: 14-bit two's complement (-8192..8191); the chip multiplies by (1 + GAN / 65536). // Channel 0 reads 0.5 % high: GAN = -0.005 * 65536 = -328. Values outside the field return false. if ( ! adc . SetChannelGain ( 0 , -328 )) { return false ; } The offset is in quarter LSBs, −512 to +511 (−128 to +127.75 LSB); the gain is signed, −8192 to +8191, and multiplies by 1 + GAN / 65536 (about ±12.5 %). A value outside its field returns false and writes nothing. Measure with the real source impedance connected: the correction is for the whole signal chain. To compute the values from two measurements, OffsetCorrectionFor(measured, expected) returns 4 × (expected − measured) (Equation 1) and GainCorrectionFor(measured, expected) returns (expected − measured) / measured × 65536 , rounded (Equation 3). Measure the gain point after the offset is corrected, with the gain correction at 0: // AIN1 shorted reads +10 LSB; with 4.5 V applied on the ±5 V range it reads 29000 instead of // 29491 (4.5 / 5 * 32768). The helpers apply Equations 1 and 3 of the datasheet. const int32_t ofs = ads9324 :: OffsetCorrectionFor ( 10 , 0 ); // -40 quarter LSBs const int32_t gan = ads9324 :: GainCorrectionFor ( 29000 - 10 , 29491 ); // measured after the offset if ( ofs < ads9324 :: kOffsetMin || ofs > ads9324 :: kOffsetMax || gan < ads9324 :: kGainMin || gan > ads9324 :: kGainMax ) { return false ; // error too large for the registers } return adc . SetChannelOffset ( 0 , static_cast < int16_t > ( ofs )) && adc . SetChannelGain ( 0 , static_cast < int16_t > ( gan )); SetSystemCorrection(offset, gain) switches the application of all offset or all gain registers on or off ( OFS_CORR_DIS and GAN_CORR_DIS in the GEN_CFG5 register of both channel banks, sections 7.3.8 and 7.3.9); both are on at reset and the register values are kept while off. On-chip ADC calibration ¶ // On-chip ADC_CAL: the inputs are disconnected for about 125 ms while the chip measures its own // offset and gain error. Run it after configuring the channels (it reads their input types). if ( ! adc . RunAdcCalibration ( ads9324 :: AdcCalMode :: OffsetAndGain )) { return false ; // bus error, or CALIB_BUSY did not clear } // The correction stays applied until a reset or until it is switched off: // adc.RunAdcCalibration(ads9324::AdcCalMode::Disabled); RunAdcCalibration(mode) runs the chip's ADC_CAL module once in single-shot mode (section 7.3.10). It turns the digital filters off and sets INT_TRIG_MODE , writes ADC_CAL_MODE and the bank input types ( SE_DIFF_MODE_AIN1_8 , SE_DIFF_MODE_AIN9_16 ), pulses ADC_CAL_TRIG for 10 µs, gives CONVST one high-low-high pulse, waits ADC_CAL_WAIT_MS (125 ms, Table 7-7) and polls CALIB_BUSY_FLAG in DEVICE_STATUS for up to ADC_CAL_TIMEOUT_MS . Then CONVST returns low and the oversampling filter is restored. A bank counts as differential when all its eight channels are; RunAdcCalibration(mode, ain1_8, ain9_16) sets the two input types yourself. AdcCalMode::Disabled removes the correction. A reset sets ADC_CAL back to disabled, so run it again after SoftwareReset() or HardwareReset() . Use it when you do not calibrate the system yourself; it reduces the offset error from about ±30 LSB to ±8 LSB in the datasheet's example. Read ¶ const ads9324 :: Snapshot snap = adc . ReadSnapshot (); // all 16 channels, same sampling instant if ( snap . ok ()) { for ( uint8_t ch = 0 ; ch < ads9324 :: kNumChannels ; ++ ch ) { if ( snap . hasChannel ( ch )) { std :: printf ( "AIN%u: %6d %.4f V 
 " , ch + 1U , snap . count [ ch ], static_cast < double > ( snap . voltage [ ch ])); } } } // One channel: still one full conversion; the others are discarded. const ads9324 :: ReadResult r = adc . ReadChannel ( 3 ); if ( r . ok ()) { const float again = adc . CountToVoltage ( 3 , r . count ); // same value as r.voltage ( void ) again ; } ReadSnapshot() is one CONVST edge: all channels are sampled at the same instant. valid_mask has a bit for each channel clocked out, and hasChannel(ch) tests it. ReadChannel() runs a full snapshot and keeps one channel; call ReadSnapshot() once when you need more than one. The SPI burst is 32 bytes at the default 16-bit word length. At the examples' 8 MHz clock that is 32 µs on the bus; see Hardware for the rate this allows. Change the data format and word length ¶ // Offset-binary coding on the wire; the driver still returns two's-complement counts. if ( ! adc . SetDataFormat ( ads9324 :: DataFormat :: OffsetBinary )) { return false ; } // 24-bit words on SDOUT (48-byte bursts); the driver uses the top 16 bits as the code. return adc . SetDigitalInterface ( ads9324 :: DoutLaneMode :: Lane1 , ads9324 :: DoutLength :: Bits24 , true ); Both calls rewrite GEN_CFG3. Snapshot::count stays two's complement whatever the wire format. Keep DoutLaneMode::Lane1 with data on SDOUT: ReadSnapshot() reads SDOUT only, so another lane setting stops the data from reaching it. Read fewer channels ¶ SetChannelCountMode(mode, ch_sel) writes ANA_CFG2 so the chip converts and outputs 8, 4 or 2 channels, which shortens the burst. // Eight channels, group 0: the chip sends AIN1..AIN4 and AIN13..AIN16 (Table 7-12). if ( adc . SetChannelCountMode ( ads9324 :: ChannelCountMode :: Eight , 0 )) { const ads9324 :: Snapshot snap = adc . ReadSnapshot (); // 16-byte burst if ( snap . ok () && snap . hasChannel ( 12 )) { // valid_mask = 0xF00F std :: printf ( "AIN13: %d 
 " , snap . count [ 12 ]); // stored under its own channel } } The chip outputs a fixed set of channels in these modes, taken from both ends of the device, lowest channel first (Table 7-12). ch_sel is the ADC_CH_SEL field; only its top bits pick the group: ChannelCountMode ch_sel Channels in the burst All16 (default) any AIN1 to AIN16 Eight 0b0xx / 0b1xx AIN1 to AIN4 and AIN13 to AIN16 / AIN5 to AIN12 Four 0b00x , 0b01x , 0b10x , 0b11x AIN1, 2, 15, 16 / AIN3, 4, 13, 14 / AIN5, 6, 11, 12 / AIN7 to AIN10 Two 0b000 to 0b111 AIN1 and AIN16, AIN2 and AIN15, ... AIN8 and AIN9 ReadSnapshot() stores each word under its real channel, so count[12] is AIN13 in every mode, and sets only those channels in valid_mask . reg::FrameChannel(mode, ch_sel, word) and reg::FrameChannelMask(mode, ch_sel) give the same mapping. ReadChannel() for a channel the chip does not send returns Error::SpiError . Average with oversampling ¶ SetOversampling(osr, clock) turns on the chip's block-average filter (section 7.3.11.2): each snapshot returns the mean of N conversions per channel. // Average 16 conversions per snapshot: +6.5 dB SNR on the ±5 V range, 62.5 kSPS at most (Table // 7-8). The internal clock runs the 16 conversions from one CONVST edge. if ( ! adc . SetOversampling ( ads9324 :: OversamplingRatio :: X16 )) { return false ; } const ads9324 :: Snapshot avg = adc . ReadSnapshot (); // averaged codes, same layout as before ( void ) avg ; // External clock: the driver pulses CONVST 16 times, at regular intervals (best antialiasing). if ( ! adc . SetOversampling ( ads9324 :: OversamplingRatio :: X16 , ads9324 :: OversamplingClock :: External )) { return false ; } return adc . SetOversampling ( ads9324 :: OversamplingRatio :: None ); // back to one conversion OversamplingRatio DIG_FILTER BLK_AVG_OSR SNR, ±5 V (Table 7-8) Highest output rate None (reset) 0000b 87.5 dB 1 MSPS X2 , X4 , X8 0001b , 0010b , 0100b 89.5, 91.2, 92.7 dB 500, 250, 125 kSPS X16 , X32 0111b , 1001b 94.0, 96.7 dB 62.5, 31.25 kSPS X64 , X128 1010b , 1011b 99.1, 101.6 dB 15.6, 7.8 kSPS X6 , X10 , X12 and X20 are also valid codes (Table 8-17); OversamplingSamples(osr) returns N . OversamplingClock DIG_FILTER INT_TRIG_MODE Conversions Internal (default) 1 One CONVST edge; the chip runs the other N − 1 itself (Figure 7-17) External 0 ReadSnapshot() pulses CONVST N times, 2 µs apart (Figure 7-16) The first enabling call writes GEN_CFG5 AVG_MODE_OVR_EN , then AVG_MODE , as section 7.3.11.2 requires; every enabling call then writes DIG_FILTER and pulses DIG_FILT_SYSREF 0 → 1 → 0, high for 2 µs (more than one t CONVST , Figure 7-14), to clear the accumulator. With the internal clock the DRDY timeout and the CONV_FALLBACK_US wait are multiplied by N . A reset returns the filter to None and GetOversampling() follows. A reserved code returns false . Window comparator and alarm pin ¶ // Window comparator on AIN1. Thresholds are compared with the top 8 bits of the code, so one // step is 256 LSB: +64 is +FS/2, -16 is -FS/8. Alert while AIN1 is outside that window. if ( ! adc . ProgramWindowComparator ( 0 , 64 , -16 )) { return false ; } // Route the comparator to the DRDY/ALARM pin. DRDY polling then no longer works: // give the port HasDrdy() == false, or switch back with SetAlarmPin(AlarmPinMode::Drdy). return adc . SetAlarmPin ( ads9324 :: AlarmPinMode :: DwcAlert ); AlarmPinMode DRDY/ALARM carries Drdy (default) Conversion ready, active high DwcAlert Any enabled window comparator out of its window AdcCalDone On-chip calibration finished OrMasked OR of the alarm flags selected by the mask SetAlarmPin(mode, true) inverts the pin's polarity. With the pin inverted or muxed away from Drdy , the driver's DRDY poll reads the wrong signal: give the port HasDrdy() == false for that time. Power down ¶ if ( ! adc . SetPowerDown ( true )) { // standby: AFE and reference off, about 6.5 mW return false ; } // ... later return adc . SetPowerDown ( false ); // the reference needs time to settle before accurate samples Standby powers down the analog front ends and the internal reference. The registers keep their values. The reference takes up to 30 ms to settle again (with 1 µF on REFCAP). Handle errors ¶ const ads9324 :: Snapshot snap = adc . ReadSnapshot (); switch ( snap . error ) { case ads9324 :: Error :: Ok : break ; case ads9324 :: Error :: NotInitialized : // EnsureInitialized() never succeeded adc . EnsureInitialized ( true ); break ; case ads9324 :: Error :: Timeout : // DRDY stayed low for DRDY_TIMEOUT_US std :: printf ( "no DRDY: check CONVST and the DRDY/ALARM mux 
 " ); break ; default : break ; } const ads9324 :: Diagnostics d = adc . GetDiagnostics (); // software counters, no SPI traffic std :: printf ( "snapshots %lu, errors %lu 
 " , static_cast < unsigned long > ( d . snapshots ), static_cast < unsigned long > ( d . errors )); Signal Meaning What to do EnsureInitialized() returns false Reset frame failed or DEVICE_ID was not 0x0004 Check ReadDeviceId() , then wiring and supplies Error::NotInitialized A read before a successful EnsureInitialized() Initialise first Error::Timeout DRDY did not rise within DRDY_TIMEOUT_US (1000 µs) CONVST wiring, DRDY polarity, SetAlarmPin() Error::InvalidChannel ReadChannel() with a channel above 15 Use 0 to 15 Error::SpiError The port's transfer() returned false , or the requested channel was not in the burst Check the bus; with a reduced channel-count mode, read a channel the chip sends ( table ) A configuration call returns false Channel above 15, a value outside its register field, or the port's transfer() returned false Use 0 to 15 and the documented ranges; check the bus GetDiagnostics() returns the software counters ( snapshots , errors ) and the cached interface settings without touching the bus. Bus errors The port's transfer() returns false on a bus error ( Porting ); the driver stops the call that sent the frame and leaves its cached settings unchanged. A failed transfer is the only error the bus can report: a wiring fault that still clocks bytes shows up as a wrong DEVICE_ID. Troubleshooting maps symptoms to causes.

The helpers apply Equations 1 and 3 of the datasheet. const int32_t ofs = ads9324 :: OffsetCorrectionFor ( 10 , 0 ); // -40 quarter LSBs const int32_t gan = ads9324 :: GainCorrectionFor ( 29000 - 10 , 29491 ); // measured after the offset if ( ofs < ads9324 :: kOffsetMin || ofs > ads9324 :: kOffsetMax || gan < ads9324 :: kGainMin || gan > ads9324 :: kGainMax ) { return false ; // error too large for the registers } return adc . SetChannelOffset ( 0 , static_cast < int16_t > ( ofs )) && adc . SetChannelGain ( 0 , static_cast < int16_t > ( gan )); SetSystemCorrection(offset, gain) switches the application of all offset or all gain registers on or off ( OFS_CORR_DIS and GAN_CORR_DIS in the GEN_CFG5 register of both channel banks, sections 7.3.8 and 7.3.9); both are on at reset and the register values are kept while off.

docs.text: // On-chip ADC_CAL: the inputs are disconnected for about 125 ms while the chip measures its own // offset and gain error. Run it after configuring the channels (it reads their input types). if ( ! adc . RunAdcCalibration ( ads9324 :: AdcCalMode :: OffsetAndGain )) { return false ; // bus error, or CALIB_BUSY did not clear } // The correction stays applied until a reset or until it is switched off: // adc.RunAdcCalibration(ads9324::AdcCalMode::Disabled); RunAdcCalibration(mode) runs the chip's ADC_CAL module once in single-shot mode (section 7.3.10). It turns the digital filters off and sets INT_TRIG_MODE , writes ADC_CAL_MODE and the bank input types ( SE_DIFF_MODE_AIN1_8 , SE_DIFF_MODE_AIN9_16 ), pulses ADC_CAL_TRIG for 10 µs, gives CONVST one high-low-high pulse, waits ADC_CAL_WAIT_MS (125 ms, Table 7-7) and polls CALIB_BUSY_FLAG in DEVICE_STATUS for up to ADC_CAL_TIMEOUT_MS . Then CONVST returns low and the oversampling filter is restored. A bank counts as differential when all its eight channels are; RunAdcCalibration(mode, ain1_8, ain9_16) sets the two input types yourself. AdcCalMode::Disabled removes the correction. A reset sets ADC_CAL back to disabled, so run it again after SoftwareReset() or HardwareReset() . Use it when you do not calibrate the system yourself; it reduces the offset error from about ±30 LSB to ±8 LSB in the datasheet's example.

ReadSnapshot (); // all 16 channels, same sampling instant if ( snap . ok ()) { for ( uint8_t ch = 0 ; ch < ads9324 :: kNumChannels ; ++ ch ) { if ( snap . hasChannel ( ch )) { std :: printf ( "AIN%u: %6d %.4f V \n " , ch + 1U , snap . count [ ch ], static_cast < double > ( snap . voltage [ ch ])); } } } // One channel: still one full conversion; the others are discarded. const ads9324 :: ReadResult r = adc . ReadChannel ( 3 ); if ( r . ok ()) { const float again = adc . CountToVoltage ( 3 , r . count ); // same value as r.voltage ( void ) again ; } ReadSnapshot() is one CONVST edge: all channels are sampled at the same instant. valid_mask has a bit for each channel clocked out, and hasChannel(ch) tests it. ReadChannel() runs a full snapshot and keeps one channel; call ReadSnapshot() once when you need more than one. The SPI burst is 32 bytes at the default 16-bit word length. At the examples' 8 MHz clock that is 32 µs on the bus; see Hardware for the rate this allows.

SetDataFormat ( ads9324 :: DataFormat :: OffsetBinary )) { return false ; } // 24-bit words on SDOUT (48-byte bursts); the driver uses the top 16 bits as the code. return adc . SetDigitalInterface ( ads9324 :: DoutLaneMode :: Lane1 , ads9324 :: DoutLength :: Bits24 , true ); Both calls rewrite GEN_CFG3. Snapshot::count stays two's complement whatever the wire format. docs.text: SetChannelCountMode(mode, ch_sel) writes ANA_CFG2 so the chip converts and outputs 8, 4 or 2 channels, which shortens the burst. // Eight channels, group 0: the chip sends AIN1..AIN4 and AIN13..AIN16 (Table 7-12). if ( adc . SetChannelCountMode ( ads9324 :: ChannelCountMode :: Eight , 0 )) { const ads9324 :: Snapshot snap = adc . ReadSnapshot (); // 16-byte burst if ( snap . ok () && snap . hasChannel ( 12 )) { // valid_mask = 0xF00F std :: printf ( "AIN13: %d \n " , snap . count [ 12 ]); // stored under its own channel } } The chip outputs a fixed set of channels in these modes, taken from both ends of the device, lowest channel first (Table 7-12). ch_sel is the ADC_CH_SEL field; only its top bits pick the group: ChannelCountMode ch_sel Channels in the burst All16 (default) any AIN1 to AIN16 Eight 0b0xx / 0b1xx AIN1 to AIN4 and AIN13 to AIN16 / AIN5 to AIN12 Four 0b00x , 0b01x , 0b10x , 0b11x AIN1, 2, 15, 16 / AIN3, 4, 13, 14 / AIN5, 6, 11, 12 / AIN7 to AIN10 Two 0b000 to 0b111 AIN1 and AIN16, AIN2 and AIN15, ... AIN8 and AIN9 ReadSnapshot() stores each word under its real channel, so count[12] is AIN13 in every mode, and sets only those channels in valid_mask . reg::FrameChannel(mode, ch_sel, word) and reg::FrameChannelMask(mode, ch_sel) give the same mapping. ReadChannel() for a channel the chip does not send returns Error::SpiError .

docs.text: SetOversampling(osr, clock) turns on the chip's block-average filter (section 7.3.11.2): each snapshot returns the mean of N conversions per channel. // Average 16 conversions per snapshot: +6.5 dB SNR on the ±5 V range, 62.5 kSPS at most (Table // 7-8). The internal clock runs the 16 conversions from one CONVST edge. if ( ! adc . SetOversampling ( ads9324 :: OversamplingRatio :: X16 )) { return false ; } const ads9324 :: Snapshot avg = adc . ReadSnapshot (); // averaged codes, same layout as before ( void ) avg ; // External clock: the driver pulses CONVST 16 times, at regular intervals (best antialiasing). if ( ! adc . SetOversampling ( ads9324 :: OversamplingRatio :: X16 , ads9324 :: OversamplingClock :: External )) { return false ; } return adc . SetOversampling ( ads9324 :: OversamplingRatio :: None ); // back to one conversion OversamplingRatio DIG_FILTER BLK_AVG_OSR SNR, ±5 V (Table 7-8) Highest output rate None (reset) 0000b 87.5 dB 1 MSPS X2 , X4 , X8 0001b , 0010b , 0100b 89.5, 91.2, 92.7 dB 500, 250, 125 kSPS X16 , X32 0111b , 1001b 94.0, 96.7 dB 62.5, 31.25 kSPS X64 , X128 1010b , 1011b 99.1, 101.6 dB 15.6, 7.8 kSPS X6 , X10 , X12 and X20 are also valid codes (Table 8-17); OversamplingSamples(osr) returns N . OversamplingClock DIG_FILTER INT_TRIG_MODE Conversions Internal (default) 1 One CONVST edge; the chip runs the other N − 1 itself (Figure 7-17) External 0 ReadSnapshot() pulses CONVST N times, 2 µs apart (Figure 7-16) The first enabling call writes GEN_CFG5 AVG_MODE_OVR_EN , then AVG_MODE , as section 7.3.11.2 requires; every enabling call then writes DIG_FILTER and pulses DIG_FILT_SYSREF 0 → 1 → 0, high for 2 µs (more than one t CONVST , Figure 7-14), to clear the accumulator. With the internal clock the DRDY timeout and the CONV_FALLBACK_US wait are multiplied by N . A reset returns the filter to None and GetOversampling() follows. A reserved code returns false .

DRDY polling then no longer works: // give the port HasDrdy() == false, or switch back with SetAlarmPin(AlarmPinMode::Drdy). return adc . SetAlarmPin ( ads9324 :: AlarmPinMode :: DwcAlert ); AlarmPinMode DRDY/ALARM carries Drdy (default) Conversion ready, active high DwcAlert Any enabled window comparator out of its window AdcCalDone On-chip calibration finished OrMasked OR of the alarm flags selected by the mask SetAlarmPin(mode, true) inverts the pin's polarity. ReadSnapshot (); switch ( snap . error ) { case ads9324 :: Error :: Ok : break ; case ads9324 :: Error :: NotInitialized : // EnsureInitialized() never succeeded adc . EnsureInitialized ( true ); break ; case ads9324 :: Error :: Timeout : // DRDY stayed low for DRDY_TIMEOUT_US std :: printf ( "no DRDY: check CONVST and the DRDY/ALARM mux \n " ); break ; default : break ; } const ads9324 :: Diagnostics d = adc . GetDiagnostics (); // software counters, no SPI traffic std :: printf ( "snapshots %lu, errors %lu \n " , static_cast < unsigned long > ( d . snapshots ), static_cast < unsigned long > ( d . errors )); Signal Meaning What to do EnsureInitialized() returns false Reset frame failed or DEVICE_ID was not 0x0004 Check ReadDeviceId() , then wiring and supplies Error::NotInitialized A read before a successful EnsureInitialized() Initialise first Error::Timeout DRDY did not rise within DRDY_TIMEOUT_US (1000 µs) CONVST wiring, DRDY polarity, SetAlarmPin() Error::InvalidChannel ReadChannel() with a channel above 15 Use 0 to 15 Error::SpiError The port's transfer() returned false , or the requested channel was not in the burst Check the bus; with a reduced channel-count mode, read a channel the chip sends ( table ) A configuration call returns false Channel above 15, a value outside its register field, or the port's transfer() returned false Use 0 to 15 and the documented ranges; check the bus GetDiagnostics() returns the software counters ( snapshots , errors ) and the cached interface settings without touching the bus. docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is put together: three layers, what each owns, and how one call reaches the chip. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one ADS9324 object, whose public methods are listed from inc/ads9324.hpp. The core packs 24-bit register frames, selects register banks, merges the PGA nibbles and unpacks conversion bursts. It reaches the hardware only through two CRTP contracts in inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp: SpiInterface (one transfer method) and HostInterface (CONVST, DRDY and two delays). The platform port is the only code you write: two small classes, or one class implementing both. Below it is the hardware. Drawn from: inc/ads9324.hpp ADS9324 public methods ; inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp SpiInterface, HostInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . The three layers ¶ Layer Where You change it Core : ADS9324<Spi, Host> , uses the two contracts only ads9324.hpp , ads9324.ipp Never, for a new board Contracts : SpiInterface , HostInterface , six methods of your port ads9324_spi_interface.hpp Never Platform port : your classes, over your SDK Your project Once per MCU or board ( Porting ) Everything above the port is the same on ESP32, STM32, a Linux host or the unit-test mock. That is how the host tests run the real driver code without hardware. How one call reaches the chip ¶ sequenceDiagram participant A as Application participant D as ADS9324 core participant S as Your SpiInterface participant H as Your HostInterface A->>D: ConfigureChannel(9, cfg) D->>D: channel 9 = AIN10: bank AIN9-16, local 1, odd nibble D->>S: BANK_SEL = 0x0004 (only if the bank changed) D->>S: GEN_CFG1 read command, then a dummy frame (read PGA_CONFIG) D->>S: PGA_CONFIG with the new high nibble D->>S: PGA_BW_SEL read and write D-->>A: true A->>D: ReadSnapshot() D->>H: ConvstWrite(true), DelayUs(1), ConvstWrite(false) D->>H: DrdyRead() every 1 µs until high D->>S: transfer(32 bytes) D-->>A: Snapshot: counts, volts, valid_mask Why CRTP ¶ The contracts are class template parameters, not virtual base classes. The compiler sees your port's methods directly and inlines them; the driver has no vtable, allocates nothing and needs no RTTI. The cost is that the driver type names the port: ADS9324<MySpi, MyHost> . One class can implement both contracts and be passed twice, as the ESP32 examples do. What the driver keeps in RAM ¶ The object caches the selected register bank (so a burst of writes to one bank costs one BANK_SEL frame), each channel's last ChannelConfig (for CountToVoltage() ), the data format, lane and word-length settings, the channel-count mode and two counters. It reads nothing back from the chip except DEVICE_ID and the shared PGA, bandwidth and comparator registers it read-modify-writes. docs.text: Changelog ¶ What changed in each release of the driver. Entries marked BREAKING need source changes in code that used the affected API. Unreleased ¶ Added ¶ HardwareReset() : pulses the active-low RESET pin through an optional ResetWrite(bool) hook in the host port (detected at compile time, HasHardwareReset() ), waits t PU and reprograms the chip like SoftwareReset() (SBASB22 section 7.4.1). RESET_PULSE_US (10 µs) sets the low time. SetReference(ReferenceSource) / GetReference() : REFSEL pin, internal or external reference through ANA_CFG1 (SBASB22 section 7.3.6, Table 7-3). SetOversampling(OversamplingRatio, OversamplingClock) / GetOversampling() : the block-average filter (DIG_FILTER BLK_AVG_OSR , 2 to 128 samples) with the internal or the external oversampling clock, including the GEN_CFG5 AVG_MODE_OVR_EN / AVG_MODE initialisation and the DIG_FILT_SYSREF accumulator reset, held high for more than one t CONVST (SBASB22 section 7.3.11.2, Figure 7-14, Table 7-8, Table 8-17, Table 8-18). ReadSnapshot() pulses CONVST N times with the external clock and scales its DRDY timeout and fallback wait by N with the internal clock. RunAdcCalibration(AdcCalMode[, InputType, InputType]) / GetAdcCalMode() : runs the on-chip ADC_CAL module in single-shot mode (offset, gain or both; SBASB22 section 7.3.10 steps 1 to 7, Table 7-7, Table 8-16), polling CALIB_BUSY_FLAG (Table 8-19) and restoring the oversampling filter afterwards. New ADC_CAL_WAIT_MS (125) and ADC_CAL_TIMEOUT_MS (125) settings. SetSystemCorrection(offset, gain) : OFS_CORR_DIS / GAN_CORR_DIS in the GEN_CFG5 register of both channel banks (SBASB22 sections 7.3.8 and 7.3.9, Table 8-70, Table 8-121). OffsetCorrectionFor() and GainCorrectionFor() compute OFS_AINn and GAN_AINn from a measurement (Equations 1 and 3). GetDriverVersion() : the version string. Host-test workflow ( ci-host-tests.yml ): GCC and Clang build and run the protocol tests and compile the documentation's code. Fixed ¶ The CONFIG_ADS9324_RANGE_* , CONFIG_ADS9324_SINGLE_ENDED and CONFIG_ADS9324_PGA_WIDE defaults only seeded the driver's channel cache; the chip kept its reset state (±5 V differential, low bandwidth), so voltages were scaled with the wrong range. EnsureInitialized() and SoftwareReset() now write them to all 16 channels (PGA_CONFIG and PGA_BW_SEL of both banks). SoftwareReset() also resets the cached channel-count mode and PGA configuration to match the chip. New DefaultChannelConfig() and CONFIG_ADS9324_RANGE_6V25 . BREAKING ReadSnapshot() in a reduced channel-count mode ( SetChannelCountMode() with Eight , Four or Two ) stored the n th word of the burst as channel n . The chip sends a fixed set from both ends of the device (SBASB22 Table 7-12, e.g. AIN1 to AIN4 and AIN13 to AIN16), so count[4] held AIN13 and was converted with channel 4's range. Each word is now stored under its real channel and valid_mask marks those channels. New helpers reg::FrameChannel() , reg::FrameChannelMask() and reg::FrameChannelCount() . Code that read the reduced burst from count[0] to count[n - 1] must read the real channels ( hasChannel() ). BREAKING GetDriverVersionMajor() , GetDriverVersionMinor() and GetDriverVersionPatch() returned the literals 1, 0, 0 whatever the project version. They now return the macros of the generated ads9324_version.h , which comes from the version in cmake/hf_ads9324_build_settings.cmake , now also the CMake project() version. ads9324.hpp includes ads9324_version.h , so a build that adds only inc/ and src/ to the include path must also add the generated header (the CMake target and the ESP-IDF component provide it). Host tests check the getters, idf_component.yml and the Doxyfile against the project version. cmake --install did not install ads9324.ipp , which ads9324.hpp includes, and exported the target as hf::hf_ads9324 while the documentation links hf::ads9324 : an installed package could not be used. The .ipp is now installed next to the headers and the target is exported as hf::ads9324 ( hf::hf_ads9324 stays as an alias). New host test hf_ads9324_install_consumer installs the package and builds a find_package() consumer. Changed ¶ BREAKING SetChannelGain(channel, gain) takes a signed int16_t (was uint16_t ): GAN_AINn is 14-bit two's complement (SBASB22 Table 7-6, Table 8-40). Values outside kGainMin (−8192) to kGainMax (+8191) are rejected with false instead of being truncated to 14 bits (8192 used to become −8192). Code that passed a negative value cast to uint16_t keeps working; code that passed the raw 14-bit pattern of a negative value (e.g. 0x3333 ) must pass the signed value (−3277). BREAKING SetChannelOffset() rejects values outside the 10-bit field, kOffsetMin (−512) to kOffsetMax (+511), instead of truncating them (512 used to become −128 LSB): such calls now return false and write nothing. BREAKING The SPI port's transfer() now returns bool ( true = bytes clocked, false = bus error) and the driver propagates it: configuration calls return false , ReadDeviceId() returns 0, ReadSnapshot() / ReadChannel() return Error::SpiError . Cached settings (data format, lanes, channel-count mode, PGA) change only after the frames that set them were transferred, and a failed BANK_SEL frame forces the next access to select the bank again. A port with a void transfer() still compiles and is treated as never failing; any other return type (for example esp_err_t ) is a compile error: return bool ( true on success). The ESP32 example port returns false on an ESP-IDF error. ESP32 examples: CI now builds basic_snapshot and pga_offset as well ( ci_enabled: true ). Both check the bool results of the configuration calls; pga_offset reads both channels from one snapshot and programs a signed gain. driver_integration_test adds oversampling, system-correction and ADC_CAL tests and logs the driver version. Documentation moved to the HardFOC MkDocs platform: new page set (quickstart, hardware, architecture, API guide, porting, testing), code snippets compiled by the host build from tests/docs/ , Doxygen under /api/ , versioned with mike. The Jekyll site files and the vendored doxygen-awesome stylesheet are gone. Host tests moved into tests/CMakeLists.txt ; the option is still HF_ADS9324_BUILD_HOST_TESTS . 1.0.0 ¶ First version (not tagged). ads9324::ADS9324<Spi, Host> : initialisation with the 1-lane SDOUT sequence of SBASB22 Table 7-18 and a DEVICE_ID check, per-channel PGA range, input type and bandwidth, offset and gain registers, data format, channel-count mode, power-down, DRDY/ALARM mux, digital window comparator, simultaneous snapshots. CRTP SpiInterface and HostInterface contracts. ESP32-C6 examples ( driver_integration_test , basic_snapshot , pga_offset ) and host protocol tests.

BREAKING ReadSnapshot() in a reduced channel-count mode ( SetChannelCountMode() with Eight , Four or Two ) stored the n th word of the burst as channel n . The chip sends a fixed set from both ends of the device (SBASB22 Table 7-12, e.g. AIN1 to AIN4 and AIN13 to AIN16), so count[4] held AIN13 and was converted with channel 4's range. Each word is now stored under its real channel and valid_mask marks those channels. New helpers reg::FrameChannel() , reg::FrameChannelMask() and reg::FrameChannelCount() . Code that read the reduced burst from count[0] to count[n - 1] must read the real channels ( hasChannel() ). BREAKING GetDriverVersionMajor() , GetDriverVersionMinor() and GetDriverVersionPatch() returned the literals 1, 0, 0 whatever the project version. They now return the macros of the generated ads9324_version.h , which comes from the version in cmake/hf_ads9324_build_settings.cmake , now also the CMake project() version. ads9324.hpp includes ads9324_version.h , so a build that adds only inc/ and src/ to the include path must also add the generated header (the CMake target and the ESP-IDF component provide it). The .ipp is now installed next to the headers and the target is exported as hf::ads9324 ( hf::hf_ads9324 stays as an alias). New host test hf_ads9324_install_consumer installs the package and builds a find_package() consumer.

docs.text: BREAKING SetChannelGain(channel, gain) takes a signed int16_t (was uint16_t ): GAN_AINn is 14-bit two's complement (SBASB22 Table 7-6, Table 8-40). Values outside kGainMin (−8192) to kGainMax (+8191) are rejected with false instead of being truncated to 14 bits (8192 used to become −8192). Code that passed a negative value cast to uint16_t keeps working; code that passed the raw 14-bit pattern of a negative value (e.g. 0x3333 ) must pass the signed value (−3277). BREAKING SetChannelOffset() rejects values outside the 10-bit field, kOffsetMin (−512) to kOffsetMax (+511), instead of truncating them (512 used to become −128 LSB): such calls now return false and write nothing. BREAKING The SPI port's transfer() now returns bool ( true = bytes clocked, false = bus error) and the driver propagates it: configuration calls return false , ReadDeviceId() returns 0, ReadSnapshot() / ReadChannel() return Error::SpiError . Cached settings (data format, lanes, channel-count mode, PGA) change only after the frames that set them were transferred, and a failed BANK_SEL frame forces the next access to select the bank again. A port with a void transfer() still compiles and is treated as never failing; any other return type (for example esp_err_t ) is a compile error: return bool ( true on success). The ESP32 example port returns false on an ESP-IDF error. ESP32 examples: CI now builds basic_snapshot and pga_offset as well ( ci_enabled: true ). Both check the bool results of the configuration calls; pga_offset reads both channels from one snapshot and programs a signed gain. driver_integration_test adds oversampling, system-correction and ADC_CAL tests and logs the driver version. Documentation moved to the HardFOC MkDocs platform: new page set (quickstart, hardware, architecture, API guide, porting, testing), code snippets compiled by the host build from tests/docs/ , Doxygen under /api/ , versioned with mike. The Jekyll site files and the vendored doxygen-awesome stylesheet are gone. Host tests moved into tests/CMakeLists.txt ; the option is still HF_ADS9324_BUILD_HOST_TESTS .

Run-time settings (range, input type, bandwidth, offset, gain, data format) are method calls; the API guide covers them. The macros below only change the values the driver starts with. They are read in inc/ads9324_config.hpp into the ADS9324_CFG namespace. Defaults ¶ Each macro below is CONFIG_ADS9324_ followed by the name in the first column. Name Effect; default without it RANGE_12V5 , RANGE_10V , RANGE_6V25 , RANGE_2V5 Range written to every channel at initialisation, DEFAULT_RANGE ; ±5 V SINGLE_ENDED Input type written to every channel, DEFAULT_INPUT_TYPE ; differential PGA_WIDE Filter written to every channel, DEFAULT_BANDWIDTH ; low bandwidth OFFSET_BINARY Data format written to GEN_CFG3 at initialisation, DEFAULT_FORMAT ; two's complement SKIP_DEVICE_ID_CHECK EnsureInitialized() stops requiring DEVICE_ID = 0x0004 ; check on POWER_ON_DELAY_MS Wait before the first frame, in ms; 30 (t PU ) RESET_DELAY_MS Wait after the software reset, in ms; 1 RESET_PULSE_US How long HardwareReset() holds RESET low, in µs; 10 (the datasheet gives no minimum) DRDY_TIMEOUT_US DRDY poll budget after CONVST, in 1 µs steps, times N with internal-clock oversampling; 1000 ADC_CAL_WAIT_MS Wait after triggering RunAdcCalibration() before checking CALIB_BUSY, in ms; 125 (T WAIT , Table 7-7) ADC_CAL_TIMEOUT_MS Further CALIB_BUSY poll budget, in 1 ms steps; 125 CONV_FALLBACK_US Wait after CONVST when HasDrdy() is false , in µs, times N with internal-clock oversampling; 10 EnsureInitialized() and SoftwareReset() write the range, input type and bandwidth defaults to all 16 channels (the PGA_CONFIG and PGA_BW_SEL registers of both channel banks) and to the driver's cache, so the chip and the voltage conversion agree without a ConfigureAllChannels() call. docs.text: Hardware ¶ What to connect between your MCU and an ADS9324, with which bus settings, and the board-level details that decide whether the first read works. All values here come from the ADS9324 datasheet (SBASB22, December 2025). When they disagree with a board's schematic, the schematic wins for pin numbers; the datasheet wins for limits. Host interface pins ¶ The driver uses the register SPI port for everything: register frames on SDI, register read-back and conversion data on SDOUT. The eight parallel data lanes stay unused. Signal (pin), direction Notes SCLK (37), in SPI clock; idles low SDI (36), in Latched on the SCLK rising edge SDOUT (38), out Register data and 1-lane conversion data; Hi-Z while CS is high CS (35), in Active low; a register write is decoded on the CS rising edge D0 to D7 (46 to 39), out Parallel data lanes, not used by the driver Control pins ¶ Pin (number) What it does Driver use CONVST (50), in The falling edge samples all channels ConvstWrite() : high for 1 µs, then low DRDY/ALARM (49), out Data ready, active high by default; can carry the window-comparator alert instead DrdyRead() , polled every 1 µs up to DRDY_TIMEOUT_US RESET (32), in Active-low asynchronous reset Optional: tie it high (to IOVDD), or wire a GPIO and give the port ResetWrite() for HardwareReset() REFSEL (31), in High: internal 4.096 V reference. Low: external reference on REFIO Not driven: tie it high for the internal reference, or override it with SetReference() EnsureInitialized() resets the chip with the SW_RST bit in GEN_CFG1, so the RESET pin can stay high. If you leave REFSEL low without an external reference on REFIO, the chip powers down (SBASB22 section 7.3.6); SetReference(ReferenceSource::Internal) selects the internal reference whatever the pin says. Bus settings ¶ Setting Value Mode SPI mode 0 (CPOL = 0, CPHA = 0), MSB first: SDI is latched on the rising edge, SCLK ends low before CS rises Clock Up to 60 MHz (f SCLK ); the ESP32-C6 examples use 8 MHz Register frame 24 bits: 8-bit address, 16-bit data; CS low for the whole frame Conversion read One CS-low burst: 16 bits per channel, 32 bytes for 16 channels (48 bytes with 24-bit words) Chip select High at least 16 ns between frames; 16 ns setup to the first edge and hold after the last I/O levels V IH ≥ 0.7 × IOVDD, V IL ≤ 0.3 × IOVDD The mode follows from the timing requirements (SDI captured on the rising edge, CS hold measured from the last falling edge); the datasheet does not name an SPI mode. Throughput in 1-lane mode ¶ Sixteen 16-bit words on one lane take 256 SCLK cycles. At the 60 MHz maximum that is 4.3 µs per snapshot, so 1-lane mode cannot exceed about 230 kSPS per channel, not the chip's 1 MSPS; at 8 MHz it is 32 µs, under 31 kSPS. These figures count clock cycles only; the conversion time, CS gaps and software overhead lower them further. Fewer channels ( SetChannelCountMode() ) or the parallel lanes raise the rate; the driver supports only 1-lane capture. One snapshot on the wire ¶ sequenceDiagram participant H as Host (driver) participant C as ADS9324 H->>C: CONVST high, 1 µs, then low (all 16 channels sampled) Note over C: conversion, t_CONV = 1.25 µs C-->>H: DRDY rises H->>C: CS low, 256 SCLK with SDI = 0 C-->>H: SDOUT: AIN1, AIN2 ... AIN16, 16 bits each, MSB first H->>C: CS high Timing ¶ Parameter Value Where the driver handles it Power-up time t PU (1 µF on REFCAP) 30 ms EnsureInitialized() waits POWER_ON_DELAY_MS = 30 Wait after software reset 1 ms (optional, Table 7-18) RESET_DELAY_MS = 1 CONVST high and low time at least 50 ns each The driver holds CONVST high for 1 µs Conversion time t CONV , no oversampling 1.25 µs DRDY poll, or CONV_FALLBACK_US = 10 µs without DRDY Conversion with oversampling ratio N N conversions (output rate 1 MSPS / N , Table 7-8) Internal clock: DRDY timeout and fallback wait times N ; external clock: N CONVST pulses 2 µs apart ADC_CAL time T WAIT , single-shot 125 ms (Table 7-7) RunAdcCalibration() waits ADC_CAL_WAIT_MS , then polls CALIB_BUSY CONVST rate f CONVST 0.1 MHz to 1 MHz See the note below Sampling rate and the specifications The datasheet specifies the ADC for a CONVST rate of 100 kHz to 1 MHz. ReadSnapshot() issues one CONVST per call, so a slow polling loop runs the chip below that range. The conversions still complete; the datasheet's dynamic performance figures are not guaranteed there. Power ¶ Supply (pins) Range Current at full rate, typ / max AVDD_5V (26, 27, 56) 4.75 V to 5.25 V 30 mA / 35 mA AVDD_1V8 (30, 51) 1.7 V to 1.9 V 32 mA / 38 mA IOVDD (34, 47) 1.7 V to 3.6 V 6 mA / 10 mA Total dissipation is 230 mW typical, 295 mW maximum, at full throughput; standby ( SetPowerDown(true) ) is about 6.5 mW. There is no power-up sequence requirement. Decouple each supply pin with 1 µF and 0.1 µF to GND. Match IOVDD to your MCU's I/O voltage. The reference needs 4.7 µF from REFIO to REFM (pin 53) and 1 µF X7R between REFCAPA and REFM (pins 52 and 53) and between REFCAPB and REFM (pins 29 and 28). Connect REFM, GND and the thermal pad to the ground plane. Analog inputs ¶ Limit Value Input impedance 1 MΩ typical (0.8 MΩ to 1.2 MΩ) on each of AIN n P and AIN n M Full-scale ranges (AIN n P − AIN n M) ±2.5, ±5, ±6.25, ±10, ±12.5 V Common-mode range, differential ±12.5 V Operating input voltage, differential –17 V to +17 V on each pin Operating input voltage, single-ended AIN n P –13 V to +13 V, AIN n M –0.5 V to +0.5 V Absolute maximum, AIN n P and AIN n M ±18 V; 10 mA per pin Low-pass filter (–3 dB) 25.5 kHz (low bandwidth) or 280 kHz to 350 kHz (wide, by range) Match the source resistance on AIN n P with the same resistance on AIN n M to cancel the offset it adds. docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake or ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 12+ or a current MSVC. No RTOS, heap or exceptions: every driver call is noexcept and returns bool or a result struct. Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to a version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-ads9324-driver.git external/hf-ads9324-driver git submodule update --init external/hf-ads9324-driver Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples have their own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ); you do not need it to use the driver. CMake ¶ add_subdirectory ( external/hf-ads9324-driver ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE hf::ads9324 ) hf::ads9324 is an INTERFACE target: it carries the include directories ( inc/ , src/ for ads9324.ipp , and the generated version header) and requires C++20 ( cxx_std_20 ), so your target does not need to set either. docs.text: PGA and calibration ¶ What each channel's analog front end can be set to, how the driver encodes it, and how to use the offset and gain correction registers. Table and equation numbers refer to the ADS9324 datasheet (SBASB22). Input type and range ¶ Each channel has its own PGA. ChannelConfig::type and ChannelConfig::range select it (Table 7-1): InputType CM_RANGE Input Differential (default) 000b AIN n P − AIN n M, common mode up to ±12.5 V SingleEnded 101b AIN n P against AIN n M at ground (±0.5 V) SingleEndedOpenWireSafe 110b Single-ended; with a pull-down on AIN n P, a disconnected source reads closest to code 0 (section 7.3.7) InputRange INPUT_RANGE Full scale (V) 1 LSB (µV) PlusMinus2V5 010b ±2.5 76.3 PlusMinus5V (default) 000b ±5 152.6 PlusMinus6V25 011b ±6.25 190.7 PlusMinus10V 100b ±10 305.2 PlusMinus12V5 101b ±12.5 381.5 1 LSB is 2 × FS / 65536. Every range is bipolar; the driver converts a count with V = count × FS / 32768 ( TwosToVoltage() ), using the range it last wrote to that channel. ChannelConfig::common_mode_correct sets CME_CORR_EN , the common-mode error correction the datasheet uses for its CMRR figures. How a channel is written ¶ Two channels share one PGA_CONFIG_AINx_y register, one byte each: Bits (per byte) Field 7 CME_CORR_EN 6:4 CM_RANGE[2:0] 3 reserved 2:0 INPUT_RANGE[2:0] The even local channel (AIN1, AIN3 ...) is the low byte, the odd one the high byte. ConfigureChannel() reads the register, replaces its byte and writes it back, then does the same with its two bits of PGA_BW_SEL . Configuring one channel therefore never changes its neighbour. Filter bandwidth ¶ ChannelConfig::bandwidth sets the low-pass filter after the PGA (Table 7-2): PgaBandwidth Range –3 dB corner Low (default) all 25.5 kHz Wide ±2.5 V 280 kHz Wide ±5 V 325 kHz Wide ±6.25 V 300 kHz Wide ±10 V, ±12.5 V 350 kHz Use Low unless the signal has content above about 10 kHz; it removes more noise and aliasing. Offset correction ¶ SetChannelOffset(channel, ofs) writes the 10-bit two's-complement OFS_AINn register. The chip adds it in quarter LSBs, before the gain (Equation 1): output = (code × 4 + OFS) / 4 OFS (register) Effect 0x1FF (+511) +127.75 LSB 0x100 (+256) +64 LSB 0x001 (+1) +0.25 LSB 0x3FF (−1) −0.25 LSB 0x200 (−512) −128 LSB To remove an offset of e LSB measured with the input shorted, write −4 × e . The range is −128 to +127.75 LSB: ofs must be between kOffsetMin (−512) and kOffsetMax (+511), otherwise the call returns false and writes nothing. Gain correction ¶ SetChannelGain(channel, gan) writes the 14-bit two's-complement GAN_AINn register; gan is a signed int16_t . The chip multiplies the offset-corrected code by 1 + GAN / 65536 (register description of GAN_AINn , Equation 2): gan GAN (register) Multiplier 0 0x0000 1.000000 (reset value) +3277 0x0CCD 1.050003 −3277 0x3333 0.949997 +8191 ( kGainMax ) 0x1FFF 1.124985 −8192 ( kGainMin ) 0x2000 0.875000 The range is about ±12.5 %. For a channel that reads a factor k too high, write GAN = −(k − 1) / k × 65536 , close to −(k − 1) × 65536 for small errors. A value outside −8192 to +8191 makes the call return false and write nothing; pass the signed value, not the register pattern (−3277, not 0x3333 ). The API guide shows both calls. On-chip calibration ¶ The ADS9324 can also measure and correct its own offset and gain ( ADC_CAL , section 7.3.10), reducing the offset error from about ±30 LSB to ±8 LSB in the datasheet's example. RunAdcCalibration() runs it once in single-shot mode: the inputs are disconnected for T WAIT = 125 ms (Table 7-7) and the correction stays applied until a reset or RunAdcCalibration(AdcCalMode::Disabled) . It is meant for systems that do not calibrate offset and gain themselves; with the system corrections above it is not needed. The API guide has the sequence. AdcCalMode ADC_CAL_MODE Calibrates Disabled (reset) 00b Nothing; no ADC_CAL correction applied Offset 01b Offset error Gain 10b Gain error OffsetAndGain 11b Both SetSystemCorrection(offset, gain) switches the OFS_AINn and GAN_AINn corrections of all channels on or off ( OFS_CORR_DIS , GAN_CORR_DIS in each bank's GEN_CFG5, Tables 8-70 and 8-121).

docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing two small classes: one for SPI, one for CONVST, DRDY and delays. The driver never calls your SDK directly. It calls six methods on classes you derive from ads9324::SpiInterface<Self> and ads9324::HostInterface<Self> (in inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp ). The base classes use CRTP: the calls are resolved at compile time, so there are no virtual functions, no vtable and nothing to allocate. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one ADS9324 object, whose public methods are listed from inc/ads9324.hpp. The core packs 24-bit register frames, selects register banks, merges the PGA nibbles and unpacks conversion bursts. It reaches the hardware only through two CRTP contracts in inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp: SpiInterface (one transfer method) and HostInterface (CONVST, DRDY and two delays). The platform port is the only code you write: two small classes, or one class implementing both. Below it is the hardware. Drawn from: inc/ads9324.hpp ADS9324 public methods ; inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp SpiInterface, HostInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . What you implement ¶ Method Class Contract transfer(tx, rx, len) SpiInterface One full-duplex transfer of len bytes with CS low for all of them. tx == nullptr : send zeros. rx == nullptr : discard the received bytes. Return true when the bytes went out, false on a bus error ConvstWrite(high) HostInterface Drive CONVST high ( true ) or low ( false ) DrdyRead() HostInterface Return true when DRDY/ALARM is high (conversion ready) HasDrdy() const HostInterface true if DRDY is wired; false makes the driver wait CONV_FALLBACK_US instead DelayUs(us) HostInterface Block for at least us microseconds (1 µs steps during the DRDY poll) DelayMs(ms) HostInterface Block for at least ms milliseconds (30 ms power-up, 1 ms after reset) ResetWrite(high) your host class, optional Drive the RESET pin: false = low (chip held in reset), true = released. Only needed for HardwareReset() The port ¶ my_port.hpp // SPI: one CS-low window per call, SPI mode 0, MSB first. class MySpi : public ads9324 :: SpiInterface < MySpi > { public : // tx == nullptr: clock out zeros. rx == nullptr: discard what arrives on SDOUT. // Return false on a bus error: the driver then fails the call that sent the frame. bool transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } }; // Host: the CONVST output, the optional DRDY input and two delays. class MyHost : public ads9324 :: HostInterface < MyHost > { public : static constexpr int kConvst = 3 ; // GPIO wired to CONVST (pin 50) static constexpr int kDrdy = 11 ; // GPIO wired to DRDY/ALARM (pin 49) static constexpr int kReset = 12 ; // GPIO wired to RESET (pin 32); optional void ConvstWrite ( bool high ) { platform_gpio_write ( kConvst , high ); } bool DrdyRead () { return platform_gpio_read ( kDrdy ); } // high = conversion done bool HasDrdy () const { return true ; } // false: fixed wait instead void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) { platform_delay_us ( us ); } void DelayMs ( uint32_t ms ) { platform_delay_us ( ms * 1000U ); } void ResetWrite ( bool high ) { platform_gpio_write ( kReset , high ); } // optional: HardwareReset() }; One class may implement both contracts; pass the same object twice: ADS9324<Bus, Bus> adc(bus, bus) . Rules for the transfer ¶ SPI mode 0 , MSB first, up to 60 MHz. Start at 1 to 8 MHz on a new board. One CS window per call. CS goes low before the first byte and high after the last. Register frames are 3 bytes; a conversion burst is 32 bytes (16 channels, 16-bit words) or 48 bytes (24-bit words). Never split one call into several CS windows: the chip decodes a register write on the CS rising edge. Handle nullptr . The driver passes real buffers today, but the contract allows either pointer to be null. Own the bus. Do not share this CS with another device, and do not let another task use the bus in the middle of a register read (two frames). transfer() returns bool : false tells the driver the transfer failed. The call that sent the frame stops there: configuration calls return false , ReadDeviceId() returns 0 and the reads return Error::SpiError . The driver's cached settings change only after the frames that set them went out, and after a failed BANK_SEL frame the next access selects the bank again. Return the SDK's status as a bool ( == ESP_OK , == HAL_OK ): any other return type is rejected at compile time, so an esp_err_t (0 = success) cannot be read as false . A port written for the earlier contract, with a void transfer() , still compiles; the driver then treats every transfer as successful. CONVST and DRDY ¶ The driver holds CONVST high for 1 µs and then drives it low; the falling edge samples every channel. The chip needs only 50 ns high and 50 ns low, so any GPIO is fast enough. DRDY is active high by default; if your board inverts it, invert it in DrdyRead() , not with SetAlarmPin(..., true) . Without DRDY ( HasDrdy() returns false ) the driver waits CONV_FALLBACK_US (10 µs) after the falling edge. The conversion takes 1.25 µs without oversampling, so the default leaves margin. Optional reset pin ¶ If RESET (pin 32) is wired to a GPIO, add void ResetWrite(bool high) to the host class, as the port above does. The driver detects it at compile time ( ADS9324<...>::HasHardwareReset() ); it is not part of HostInterface , so a port without it compiles unchanged and HardwareReset() returns false . Hold RESET high from power-up, for example with a pull-up, so the chip is not held in reset before your code runs. Reference implementation ¶ The ESP32 examples use esp32_ads9324_bus.hpp : one class that implements both contracts with the ESP-IDF spi_master driver (hardware CS, one transaction per call), GPIO for CONVST and DRDY, esp_rom_delay_us() and FreeRTOS delays. Start from it for any ESP-IDF target. Check your port ¶ Build it: the port on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/ , with the driver instantiated over it. Call EnsureInitialized() . If it fails, print ReadDeviceId() : 0x0004 proves SDI, SCLK, CS and SDOUT end to end. Short one input and read a snapshot: the count should be within a few tens of LSB of zero. Watch GetDiagnostics().errors : it should stay at zero on a healthy link. Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe. Give each ADS9324 one owner task, or guard every call on a driver object (and its port) with one mutex. Several chips on separate buses can run in parallel.

Wire it ¶ MCU ADS9324 (pin) Notes SPI SCLK SCLK (37) SPI mode 0; up to 60 MHz, start at 1 to 8 MHz SPI MOSI SDI (36) Register frames, zeros during a conversion read SPI MISO SDOUT (38) Register read-back and, in the driver's mode, conversion data SPI CS CS (35) Active low; one CS-low window per transfer GPIO out CONVST (50) The falling edge samples all channels GPIO in DRDY/ALARM (49) Optional; active high when a conversion is ready IOVDD RESET (32), REFSEL (31) RESET is active low: hold it high. REFSEL high selects the internal reference GND GND Common ground; also the thermal pad The ADS9324 needs three supplies (5 V, 1.8 V and the 1.7 V to 3.6 V I/O rail) and its reference capacitors before it answers. The Hardware page has the full pin list, the supplies and the timing. 2. Add the driver ¶ Add the repository as a submodule and link the hf::ads9324 CMake target (or add inc/ and src/ to your include path and build with C++20). Installation covers CMake and ESP-IDF. git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-ads9324-driver.git external/hf-ads9324-driver 3. Write the port ¶ The port is the only platform code: one SPI transfer, the CONVST and DRDY pins, and two delays. Replace the platform_* calls with your SDK's. my_port.hpp // SPI: one CS-low window per call, SPI mode 0, MSB first. class MySpi : public ads9324 :: SpiInterface < MySpi > { public : // tx == nullptr: clock out zeros. rx == nullptr: discard what arrives on SDOUT. // Return false on a bus error: the driver then fails the call that sent the frame. bool transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } }; // Host: the CONVST output, the optional DRDY input and two delays. class MyHost : public ads9324 :: HostInterface < MyHost > { public : static constexpr int kConvst = 3 ; // GPIO wired to CONVST (pin 50) static constexpr int kDrdy = 11 ; // GPIO wired to DRDY/ALARM (pin 49) static constexpr int kReset = 12 ; // GPIO wired to RESET (pin 32); optional void ConvstWrite ( bool high ) { platform_gpio_write ( kConvst , high ); } bool DrdyRead () { return platform_gpio_read ( kDrdy ); } // high = conversion done bool HasDrdy () const { return true ; } // false: fixed wait instead void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) { platform_delay_us ( us ); } void DelayMs ( uint32_t ms ) { platform_delay_us ( ms * 1000U ); } void ResetWrite ( bool high ) { platform_gpio_write ( kReset , high ); } // optional: HardwareReset() }; HasDrdy() returning false makes the driver wait a fixed time after CONVST instead of polling DRDY. Porting explains each method. 4. Read the channels ¶ main.cpp #include "ads9324.hpp" int read_all_16_channels ( MySpi & spi , MyHost & host ) { ads9324 :: ADS9324 < MySpi , MyHost > adc ( spi , host ); if ( ! adc . EnsureInitialized ()) { // 1. reset, 1-lane SDOUT, DEVICE_ID return -1 ; // wiring, supplies or SPI mode } ads9324 :: ChannelConfig cfg ; // 2. every input: differential, ±10 V cfg . type = ads9324 :: InputType :: Differential ; cfg . range = ads9324 :: InputRange :: PlusMinus10V ; if ( ! adc . ConfigureAllChannels ( cfg )) { return -2 ; } const ads9324 :: Snapshot snap = adc . ReadSnapshot (); // 3. CONVST, wait DRDY, read 32 bytes if ( ! snap . ok ()) { return -3 ; // snap.error says why } std :: printf ( "AIN1 = %.4f V \n " , static_cast < double > ( snap . voltage [ 0 ])); // 4. channel 0 is AIN1 return 0 ; } What each step does: EnsureInitialized() waits 30 ms for the supplies and reference, resets the chip, writes GEN_CFG3 = 0x0032 (1 lane, 16-bit words, data on SDOUT), checks DEVICE_ID = 0x0004 and writes the compile-time PGA defaults (±5 V differential unless configured ) to every channel. Nothing else works until it returns true . ConfigureAllChannels() writes each channel's PGA nibble and filter bit. The ranges are bipolar; the driver remembers them to convert counts to volts. ReadSnapshot() pulses CONVST, waits for DRDY, then clocks 32 bytes out of SDOUT in one CS-low window. Channel 0 in the API is AIN1 on the chip; channel 15 is AIN16. This example is built by the host CI, so it compiles against the current headers. If it does not work ¶ Symptom First thing to check EnsureInitialized() returns false ReadDeviceId() : 0x0000 means no SDOUT data (wiring, SPI mode, supplies); anything else but 0x0004 means a framing problem Snapshot error Timeout CONVST wiring, DRDY polarity, or set HasDrdy() to false All counts near zero Input type and range, a floating input in open-wire-safe mode, or the AIN x M pin not connected Voltages off by a fixed factor The range you configured is not the range you assumed ( PGA and calibration ) Next ¶ API guide : per-channel set-up, calibration, window comparator, errors. Examples : ESP32-C6 applications, including the integration test suite. Registers and SPI frames : what goes over the wire.

docs.text: Registers and SPI frames ¶ What the driver sends over SPI: the 24-bit register frame, the three register banks, the two-frame read and the conversion burst. Section and table numbers refer to the ADS9324 datasheet (SBASB22). The addresses are constants in inc/ads9324_registers.hpp (namespace ads9324::reg ). The register frame ¶ Every register access is one 24-bit frame, MSB first, CS low for all 24 clocks: Bits 23:16 15:0 SDI Register address 16-bit data SDI is latched on the SCLK rising edge; the write is decoded when CS rises (section 7.5.1). reg::PackWrite(addr, data) builds the frame. Register banks ¶ The 16-bit registers sit in three banks addressed with 8 bits. BANK_SEL (address 0x02 ) is reachable from every bank and selects which one later addresses decode in: BANK_SEL value Bank Holds 0x0001 Common GEN_CFG1 to GEN_CFG5, PDN_CTL, DRDY_ALARM_SEL, ANA_CFG½, ADC_CAL, DEVICE_ID 0x0002 AIN1 to AIN8 PGA_CONFIG, PGA_BW_SEL, OFS, GAN, DWC registers of channels 1 to 8 0x0004 AIN9 to AIN16 The same for channels 9 to 16 The two channel banks have the same layout. API channel n (0 to 15) is in bank AIN1-8 when n < 8, with local index n mod 8 ( reg::BankForChannel() , reg::LocalChannel() ). The driver writes BANK_SEL only when the bank changes. Reading a register ¶ A read takes two frames (Table 7-17): Frame SDI[23:16] SDI[15:0] SDOUT 1 0x01 (GEN_CFG1) REG_ADDR in bits 15:8, REG_RD_EN = 1 in bit 0 don't care 2 0x00 0x0000 Bits 23:8 = the register's data, bits 7:0 = 0 The driver selects the bank first, so a read costs two or three frames. reg::ReadCommand() and reg::UnpackRegData() build and unpack them. Registers the driver uses ¶ Common bank: Address Name Driver use 0x01 GEN_CFG1 SW_RST (bit 1) in SoftwareReset() ; register-read command 0x02 BANK_SEL Bank selection 0x08 PDN_CTL DEVICE_PDN (bit 0) in SetPowerDown() 0x0A GEN_CFG3 EN_OFS_BINARY (12), DOUT_LANE_SEL (5:4), DOUT_LENGTH (3:2), ADC_DATA_SDOUT_EN (1) 0x0C DRDY_ALARM_SEL ALRM_POL (4), DRDY_ALRM_SEL (3:0) in SetAlarmPin() 0x10 ANA_CFG1 REFSEL_CTRL_DIS (1), EXT_REF_EN (0) in SetReference() 0x11 ANA_CFG2 ADC_CH_SEL (6:4), ADC_NUM_SEL (3:2) in SetChannelCountMode() 0x12 ADC_CAL SE_DIFF_MODE_AIN1_8 (13), SE_DIFF_MODE_AIN9_16 (12), ADC_CAL_TRIG (8), ADC_CAL_MODE (1:0) in RunAdcCalibration() 0x14 DIG_FILTER BLK_AVG_OSR (7:4), INT_TRIG_MODE (1), DIG_FILT_SYSREF (0) in SetOversampling() 0x15 GEN_CFG5 AVG_MODE_OVR_EN (1), then AVG_MODE (0), before the first SetOversampling() 0x1D DEVICE_STATUS CALIB_BUSY_FLAG (3) polled by RunAdcCalibration() 0x21 DEVICE_ID Read by ReadDeviceId() ; 0x0004 on an ADS9324 Channel banks (the same address in AIN1-8 and AIN9-16): Address Name Driver use 0x08 to 0x0B PGA_CONFIG_AINx_y Two channels per register, one byte each 0x0C PGA_BW_SEL Two bits per channel 0x11 to 0x18 OFS_AINn 10-bit offset 0x19 to 0x20 GAN_AINn 14-bit gain 0x21 DWC_CFG Window-comparator enable bit per channel 0x22 to 0x29 DWC_TH_AINn High threshold (15:8), low threshold (7:0) 0x37 GEN_CFG5 OFS_CORR_DIS (1), GAN_CORR_DIS (0) in SetSystemCorrection() The other registers (FIR and moving-average filters, phase delay, test patterns) have addresses in ads9324_registers.hpp but no driver call. PGA and calibration explains the channel registers. Initialisation sequence ¶ EnsureInitialized() follows Table 7-18, checks the ID, then writes the channel defaults: Step Frame or action Why 1 Wait 30 ms Supplies and reference settle (t PU ) 2 BANK_SEL = 0x0001 , GEN_CFG1 = 0x0002 Software reset; the bank is selected first because GEN_CFG1 is in the common bank and the chip may have kept another bank across an MCU reset 3 Wait 1 ms Reset settle 4 BANK_SEL = 0x0001 Common bank 5 GEN_CFG3 = 0x0032 1 lane, 16-bit words, conversion data on SDOUT 6 Read DEVICE_ID , expect 0x0004 Proves SDI, SDOUT, SCLK and CS work 7 PGA_CONFIG_AINx_y and PGA_BW_SEL of both channel banks The CONFIG_ADS9324_* range, input type and bandwidth defaults ( Configuration ) After reset the chip outputs conversion data on eight lanes (D0 to D7), which a plain SPI controller cannot read; step 5 is what makes SDOUT carry it. The conversion burst ¶ After CONVST and DRDY, the driver clocks one CS-low burst with SDI held at zero. Each channel is one word, MSB first, lowest channel first (Figure 5-5): Setting Word Burst for 16 channels DoutLength::Bits16 (default) 16 bits 32 bytes DoutLength::Bits24 24 bits; the driver keeps the top 16 48 bytes With ADC_NUM_SEL set to 8, 4 or 2 channels the burst is shorter and carries the Table 7-12 channel set, for example AIN1 to AIN4 then AIN13 to AIN16; the driver stores each word under its channel ( API guide ). With the default two's-complement coding, 0 V is 0x0000 , the most positive code is 0x7FFF and −FS is 0x8000 . In offset-binary coding midscale is 0x8000 ; the driver converts it to two's complement, so Snapshot::count is always signed.

docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host tests against a model of the chip, compiled documentation, ESP32 builds and static analysis, on every pull request. Host tests ¶ The tests build the real driver against a mock that implements both contracts: a register file for the three banks that answers the two-frame read, a CONVST edge counter and a canned conversion burst. No hardware or ESP-IDF is needed. cmake -S . -B build-host -DHF_ADS9324_BUILD_HOST_TESTS = ON cmake --build build-host ctest --test-dir build-host --output-on-failure File Covers tests/host/test_ads9324_protocol.cpp Frame packing, GEN_CFG3 value, PGA nibble encoding, bank mapping, the initialisation sequence and DEVICE_ID, channel configuration, offset and gain registers, power-down, snapshot unpacking and the reduced channel-count layouts, ReadChannel() errors, bus-error propagation, software and hardware reset, reference selection, oversampling, ADC_CAL and the system-correction bits tests/host/test_ads9324_config_defaults.cpp Built with non-default CONFIG_ADS9324_* values: initialisation and reset write them to the chip tests/host/test_ads9324_version.cpp GetDriverVersion*() equal the project version, and follow a generated header with another version tests/check_version_copy.cmake idf_component.yml and Doxyfile carry the project version tests/install_consumer.cmake cmake --install into the build tree, then a find_package() consumer that includes every public header and links hf::ads9324 The build also compiles the protocol test at -O2 -Werror (target hf_ads9324_optimised_build , never run): GCC reports array-bounds and similar warnings only with optimisation, and the ESP-IDF Release builds treat them as errors. Documentation snippets ¶ Every C++ block on this site is included from tests/docs/ , which the host build compiles (target hf_ads9324_doc_snippets ) with the driver instantiated over the documented port. A change to the API that breaks a page breaks the build first. CI workflows ¶ Workflow What it checks Host unit tests GCC and Clang build and run the tests and the doc snippets ESP32 examples build Every CI-enabled app in examples/esp32/app_config.yml , for each listed ESP-IDF version and build type; clang-format and clang-tidy on the examples C++ lint, C++ analysis clang-format, clang-tidy and cppcheck Docs Strict site build, figure and generated-table drift, Doxygen, link check, Lighthouse budget Markdown lint, YAML lint, link check Repository text files The workflows call the shared, versioned workflows of hf-general-ci-tools and hf-espidf-ci-tools . On hardware ¶ The driver_integration_test example is the hardware test suite: it runs initialisation, PGA, snapshot, calibration and power-down tests and prints a pass / fail summary over the serial monitor.

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms you may see while bringing up an ADS9324, their causes and the fix for each, cheapest check first. Start with ReadDeviceId() and GetDiagnostics() : a correct DEVICE_ID ( 0x0004 ) proves the SPI link, so a remaining problem is in CONVST, DRDY or the channel settings. Initialisation ¶ Symptom Cause Fix ReadDeviceId() returns 0x0000 SDOUT not connected, chip not powered, RESET held low, or REFSEL low with no external reference (the chip powers down) Check the three supplies, tie RESET and REFSEL high ( Hardware ) DEVICE_ID is 0xFFFF or random Wrong SPI mode, MISO floating, CS released between bytes SPI mode 0, one CS window per transfer() , lower the clock DEVICE_ID right on the second call only The first frame went out before the supplies settled Keep POWER_ON_DELAY_MS at 30 or more; power the ADC before the MCU starts talking Snapshots ¶ Symptom Cause Fix Error::Timeout CONVST not reaching the chip, DRDY not wired, DRDY inverted, or DRDY/ALARM muxed to the comparator Scope CONVST and DRDY; SetAlarmPin(AlarmPinMode::Drdy) ; or HasDrdy() = false All counts 0 or -1 Conversion data still on D0 to D7 (8-lane reset mode), so SDOUT is idle Call EnsureInitialized() after every power cycle or hardware reset; do not change SetDigitalInterface() away from 1 lane on SDOUT A channel reads 0 and hasChannel() is false A reduced SetChannelCountMode() is active and the chip does not send that channel Pick the group that contains it, or ChannelCountMode::All16 ( API guide ) Values ¶ Symptom Cause Fix Voltage off by a fixed factor (2, 2.5, 4 ...) Your application talks to one ADS9324 object, whose public methods are listed from inc/ads9324.hpp. The core packs 24-bit register frames, selects register banks, merges the PGA nibbles and unpacks conversion bursts.
